problem_statement: The paper frames the problem as pricing complicated financial derivatives, especially in a big-data setting where derivative models involve larger-scale data and more complex payoff structures. It uses European options and defaultable bonds as examples of the kinds of derivatives being priced.
problem_statement_quotes:
Since the beginning of the 21st century, the scale and complexity
of financial derivatives have increased significantly.

Meanwhile,
the pricing models of derivatives have become increasingly com-
plex, and have involved larger-scale data, posing unprecedented
challenges to algorithms and computing speed.

This paper
takes the pricing of European options and defaultable bonds as
examples to explore the application of Quantum Monte Carlo Simu-
lation of complicated derivative pricing in big data.
classical_baseline: The paper treats the Black-Scholes-Merton model as the standard analytical baseline for simple derivatives, and Monte Carlo simulation as the classical numerical approach used when closed-form solutions are unavailable or models become too complex. For the complicated-derivative example, it compares quantum Monte Carlo against classical Monte Carlo simulation.
classical_baseline_quotes:
The famous Black-Scholes-Merton (BSM) model [1][2][3] has successfully
priced a large variety of financial derivatives

Thus, in many cases, the pricing employs Monte Carlo methods
that expend vast computational space and time.

the pricing of the defaultable bond will be conducted with
the quantum Monte Carlo simulation compared with the classical
Monte Carlo simulation on the background of big data..
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical pricing becomes difficult because many derivative models have too many parameters or no explicit solution, and Monte Carlo methods require vast computational space and time. It also says classical computing can struggle to meet real-time speed needs, especially as data scale and model complexity grow.
classical_difficulty_quotes:

Although classi-
cal computing can still solve the pricing problem of some complex

business_stakes: The paper links derivative pricing to risk management and says derivatives are used to hedge risks for financial firms and even manufacturing enterprises. It also emphasizes the need for real-time computing in big-data settings.

extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper mixes simple-option and complicated-derivative framing, but the financial problem is clear.
